strings.name: Alejandro González Iñárritu
strings.summary: Iñárritu moved from Mexican radio, music and advertising into films such as Amores perros and Babel, using interwoven stories to explore chance, class and cross-cultural connections. Birdman and The Revenant earned consecutive directing Oscars. He has also worked with long takes, virtual reality and autobiographical cinema, alongside actors, cinematographers and production teams. His black comedy Digger reached cinemas in 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Through Babel, Birdman and The Revenant, he explores cross-cultural storytelling and cinematic form, creating international influence in film.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and beginnings
strings.facts.f2.value: Attended Universidad Iberoamericana without completing a degree; early work included radio, scoring and advertising.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Consecutive directing Oscars
strings.highlights.h1.text: Won the 2015 and 2016 directing Oscars for Birdman and The Revenant respectively.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Cross-cultural and formal exploration
strings.highlights.h2.text: Explored interconnected international stories in Babel and immersive border experiences in Carne y Arena.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Digger reached cinemas
strings.timeline.t1.text: His black comedy with Tom Cruise examined contemporary power and catastrophe.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Released Bardo
strings.timeline.t2.text: The autobiographically inflected film explored memory, migration and identity.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Presented Carne y Arena
strings.timeline.t3.text: The virtual-reality border experience received a Special Achievement Academy Award.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Won another directing Oscar
strings.timeline.t4.text: Received Best Director for The Revenant, his second consecutive win.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Birdman won Academy recognition
strings.timeline.t5.text: The film won picture, directing and original-screenplay awards, with shared honors for collaborators.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Won Cannes directing award for Babel
strings.timeline.t6.text: His interconnected multinational drama won Cannes Best Director and later earned a directing Oscar nomination.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Made feature debut
strings.timeline.t7.text: Amores perros appeared in Cannes Critics’ Week and received a foreign-language Oscar nomination.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Entered radio
strings.timeline.t8.text: Began work at Mexico’s WFM, later moving into music, advertising and filmmaking.
